title: the-corpus-is-out-of-proven-space
intention: settle what proven-space IS — a state the corpus rests in, or a fresh state a component enters when it is about to be leaned on — and enforce that answer with something other than a human remembering, so the measured fraction is what the rule predicts rather than an accident of who edited what last.
why: The lived symptom arrives the first time somebody outside this voyage tries to cross into a rest: clearance demands a proof standing in proven-space, they name their component's proof, and the door tells them the seal is green but the code has moved underneath it. Their ordinary crossing has become a re-seal errand, and nothing warned them, because the corpus reads green everywhere — 78 proofs with green seals beside them, 6 of which mean what a reader assumes all 78 mean.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured — 6 of 78 is the whole content of this, and nobody had counted)
Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass — this asks what STAYING there means)
Law 9 (red is the default; green is earned — a green seal over moved code is green that stopped being earned and nothing derived red)

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam@v2 gate-set, transcribed. PROVEME (non-skippable): proofs beside the code at cairn/devices/tester/proofs/, run twice, sealed under the tester with isolation='netns' and persisted through validation_store.persist_validation. The Law 8 teeth: (i) the census that produces the number is a tooth, not a script — it asserts INVARIANTS (every non-standing proof carries a why naming which of the four ways it failed; the standing set is a subset of the sealed set) rather than the snapshot value 6, because the number legitimately moves; (ii) whatever the settled rule is, a tooth that fails if the rule is reverted; (iii) a tooth over the four broken TRAILS asserting they are diagnosed rather than overwritten — the trail file before and after is byte-identical for its existing lines. BUILD GATE: the PROVEME crossing runs build_inspector over cairn/devices/tester at its own address. FEEDBACK TO ORIGIN ON FAILURE (Law 3+8 invariant): a red routes back to this ticket and to cairn/devices/tester/intention+why.json, whose horizon is what this node is measuring against.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when the corpus has a STATED rule for what proven-space is (a resting state the corpus is held in, or a fresh state a component enters when it is about to be leaned on), that rule is enforced by something other than a human remembering, and the measured number is what the rule predicts rather than an accident. RED on any of: (1) the answer is a periodic re-seal sweep — a poll, which the standing shrinking-footprint aim refuses, and which manufactures the number it reports; (2) the number is raised by weakening standing() (dropping the fingerprint check, widening the horizon) — proven-space bought by lowering what proven means is the check going green for the wrong reason; (3) the four broken TRAILS are re-sealed rather than diagnosed, which would overwrite the evidence of a Law 7 integrity failure with a fresh green; (4) the rule lands and the number does not move, meaning the rule was written to describe what already happens. HORIZON: the first crossing that is REFUSED for an unproven proven_by after this ticket proves out. Until one exists, the rule is unexercised and its cost is unmeasured — and its cost is the whole question, because a seal decayed at the moment somebody needs it turns an ordinary crossing into a re-seal errand.

how: Settle what proven-space IS (a resting state or a fresh entry state). Enforce the answer: four seal trails that do not verify, and the leaning-on that depends on the answer. Children decompose the definition and the four trails.
